soldier.title: One More Place
soldier.body: Mara leaves the roll book open beside the gate. In the old watch, a blank line meant someone had failed to report. Tonight she draws a little chair beside each empty space. A child asks who the chairs are for. Anyone who comes late, she says. By dawn there are cups beside them. Someone has found a table. The book no longer looks like a list of people missing. It looks like a place being set.

medic.title: Clean Bandages
medic.body: Iona washes the last bandage until the water runs clear. The name written on it will not come out. She folds it carefully anyway. Outside, a former patient has opened a stall that sells broth for buttons, stories, or nothing at all. He calls her over to settle an argument about salt. For the first time in months, nobody is asking her who can be saved. They are asking how she likes her supper.

heavy.title: The Quiet Shift
heavy.body: Hux takes the feed motor apart and finds a child's wooden horse wedged behind the governor. Someone hid it there before the foundry closed. He spends the afternoon carving a missing wheel from a packing crate. The machine can wait. When the horse rolls down the workbench, three survivors cheer as if a bell has fallen. Hux puts the motor back together after supper. This time he leaves a switch within everyone's reach.

tank.title: A Door on Hinges
tank.body: Bram finds a frame that fits the door he has carried through half the city. He measures it twice. The others expect him to mount it across the last breach, but he chooses a small house beside the infirmary instead. He spends an hour making certain it opens without a sound. There, he says, trying the handle. A door should be easy to open from the inside. He leaves the key in the lock.

mage.title: A Useful Margin
mage.body: Sable's notebook contains eleven ways to silence a bell and no instructions for teaching someone to read. She turns it upside down and begins at the back. By evening the forbidden harmonics have acquired a border of crooked letters. One pupil writes her own name so large it crosses a theorem. Sable considers correcting it, then rules two more lines underneath. There is room. The notebook was always supposed to explain what people could do together.

engineer.title: Borrowed Parts
engineer.body: Tamsin builds a pump from a clock case, a kettle lid, and a spring Hux swears he does not need. It leaks in six places. She writes each leak on the wall and asks who wants to take one. By morning, six different repairs hold. No two look alike. The water reaches the upstairs rooms for the first time since quarantine. Tamsin crosses out her name on the drawing and writes all seven names beneath it.

assassin.title: Return Address
assassin.body: Vale has carried the same undelivered letter since the streets went quiet. Its house number is gone, so they pin it to a board outside the gate. Other letters appear beside it. Someone adds a map. Someone else adds a bench for the people who stop to look. Three days later the envelope is missing and a small blue ribbon is tied through its pinhole. Vale leaves the ribbon where it is. The route is open.

bard.title: The Second Verse
bard.body: Iven finds the loose reed while putting the concertina away. He has played around its buzz for three evenings. In the hall, he would have blamed the room before admitting it was his instrument. This time he lays it on the table. A woman who has been listening asks whether she may try the phrase. She plays it more slowly than he does, stopping where he usually fills the silence. Someone at the other end of the table supplies a word. It is an ordinary word, about an ordinary supper. Iven leaves it in. He will have to mend the reed in the morning.
